dedupe_keys.name: mass evacuation clearance time after a large scale chemical accident in ulsan transims agent based model with aloha 2020

description: This case study builds a modelling framework for mass evacuation after a large-scale chemical accident by coupling the TRANSIMS agent-based traffic model with the ALOHA toxic gas dispersion model. The baseline scenario assumes toxic chemicals leak at once from the 51 chemical plants in the two national industrial complexes of Ulsan, a South Korean metropolitan area of 1.17 million people, with threat zones set by emergency response planning guidelines. ALOHA showed that about 60% of residents would have to leave their homes; in the baseline, with as many private cars as possible and no intervention, most evacuees finished within five hours, while population distribution and street network density made clearance times vary across the city. Alternative scenarios showed that changing evacuee behaviour and evacuation policy can cut clearance time considerably. It was written by Minjun Kim and Gi-Hyoug Cho and published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health on 16 December 2020. Coverage is one city. The article is available free online under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: a simultaneous release from all plants is an extreme assumption, and the model inputs are not published. For simulation it is a worked example of coupling dispersion and traffic agent models to test evacuation policies around chemical plants. It is related to the Ulsan chlorine leak selective evacuation case study record in this catalogue.
